question:
In the given diagram of an adjustable jack stand, what is the name of the part marked as ‘X’?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b839ce405843cc5ca6d9387208d14d53a4a839ae79ec11235d7b5f61d7c1bd1.png]
solution:
The correct answer is __Ratchet teeth**(Option 3)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ratchet teeth__ are the notched parts of a ratchet mechanism that allow movement in one direction while preventing movement in the opposite direction.
 
• They are a crucial component in the adjustable jack stand to lock it securely in place.
 
• The design of the ratchet teeth ensures incremental height adjustments and stability of the jack stand.
 
• This mechanism is widely used in tools, machinery, and equipment that require controlled, unidirectional movement.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Outlet valve:**

 
 
• This is a component often found in hydraulic systems, used to release pressure or fluid.
 
• It is not typically associated with the mechanical locking mechanism of a jack stand.
 
 
 
• **Ratchet handle:**
 
 
• The ratchet handle is used to operate the ratchet mechanism, usually in tools like socket wrenches.
 
• In the context of a jack stand, it is not the part that locks the stand at a set height.
 
 
 
• **Saddle:**
 
 
• The saddle is the part of the jack stand that supports the weight of the load.
 
• It is not related to the locking mechanism of the stand.
